newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-May 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-May 1.

text.p: There are 61 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- The MING PAO DAILY said there were many flaws in the proposal to amend two civil rights ordinances, which needed to be improved. It said most Hong Kong people hoped that their present freedoms would remain unchanged, and that Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa had to accept the result of the consultation exercise.

-- The Beijing-backed WEN WEI PO said that the discussion between Hong Kong and Taiwan over shipping after the handover should not be politicised, because maintaining shipping was to the benefit of people in both places. The paper urged the Taiwan authorities to adopt a pragmatic attitude when handling the issue and respect the laws and regulations of the future Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

-- The English-language HONG KONG STANDARD said the consultation document produced by the Chief Executive's office which proposed to amend two civil rights laws were more noted for its utter lack of precision and research than good intentions. The focus should have been on what was in Hong Kong's best interests. The Chief Executive's office must pay heed to public opinion and the general sentiment of Hong Kong people when finalising the details of the bill.
